text:
Seattle spent most of Saturday afternoon in Helsinki watching the champions play keep-away. Carolina out-attempted Seattle 96 to 28 at Veikkaus Arena, scored three times on the power play and finished a Global Series sweep with a 5-1 win, its fourth straight.

Joey Daccord kept it level early, including a stop on Jackson Blake's 22% look in the first period, but the dam broke at 11:12 when Blake snapped home a power-play goal from Sebastian Aho and Nikolaj Ehlers. That lifted Carolina's win chance from 54% to 70%. Mark Jankowski made it 2-0 at 17:30 on a shot that goes in about 6% of the time, and the Hurricanes had built a 1.90 to 0.31 edge in expected goals (the quality of their chances) by intermission.

Andrei Svechnikov took over the second. He scored on the power play 2:03 in, Matty Beniers answered with a slap shot at 6:06 that briefly nudged Seattle's chances from 6% to 15%, and Svechnikov restored the three-goal lead with another power-play slapper at 10:05. Ehlers had a hand in all three power-play goals, and Shayne Gostisbehere assisted on both of Svechnikov's. Daccord finished with four goals allowed on 14 shots.

Philipp Grubauer was very good in relief, stopping 22 of 23 and saving 1.7 goals more than his shots deserved, including Jankowski's 31% chance in the third. Jankowski got his second anyway at 11:06, a wrister set up by Taylor Hall and Seth Jarvis. Two goals on 0.76 expected goals made him the first star. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 12 saves on 13 shots.

By our numbers, this was as one-sided as it looked: 5.29 expected goals to 1.22, and Carolina deserved to win 96% of the time if you replayed every shot. For Seattle, that's three losses in a row with two of them in Finland against the team that won the Cup in June.
headline: Svechnikov, Jankowski finish Carolina's sweep in Helsinki
